node.statement: Replace the final norm chain by the following fully non-strict argument. Let V=i*reals*J and q:icalH->icalH/V be the quotient map. With R=DF_+(0)+I=D(F_+-id)(0)+2I, the preceding vertical calculation gives R|_V=0, so Rbar(q(x)):=q(Rx) is well-defined and equals D-breve-sigma_{breve-e}+I. For every x in icalH and v in V, Rbar(q(x))=q(R(x+v)); hence ||Rbar(q(x))||_quot<=||R(x+v)||<=||R||*||x+v||. Infimizing over v gives ||Rbar(q(x))||_quot<=||R||*||q(x)||_quot and therefore ||Rbar||<=||R||. Assumption (A_7), evaluated at A=0, gives ||R||=||D(F_+-id)(0)+2I||<=C_der*(epsilon_r+r_iso), while (R) gives C_der*(epsilon_r+r_iso)<=kappa_der/4<1. Consequently ||D-breve-sigma_{breve-e}+I||=||Rbar||<=||R||<=C_der*(epsilon_r+r_iso)<=kappa_der/4<1. This uses no unsupported strict inequality and proves the required strict conclusion.
